clue.text: Lacking gravity this Dickensian would be uncouth

indicators.note: the clue says the name, minus the gravity letter, would be the uncouth word, so the solver sets that letter within it

parts.note: uncouth means rude, ill-mannered
the missing piece is the gravity letter, G, the physics symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A Dickens character without any seriousness would come across as boorish.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs in reverse: take G (gravity) out of the Dickensian's name and what is left 'would be' RUDE, so the solver puts G into RUDE. Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge is the title hero of a Charles Dickens novel, so his surname names a Dickensian figure.

clue.text: One whose recovery wins the game

definitions.text: One whose recovery wins the game

parts.words: One whose recovery wins the game
parts.note: read as a sportsman whose comeback wins a match, but it is a gundog that recovers (fetches) shot game birds

explanation.definitionFit: A gun dog is bred to fetch shot birds, recovering the game for the shooter.

clue.text: They come up for the pools punter, or the turf

definitions.text: They come up for the pools punter

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading the word from the bottom upwards

parts.note: sward is grassy turf

explanation.surface: Something a football pools gambler hopes for, or else the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: On the football pools (a British betting game on match results) score draws are what punters hope will 'come up'; 'come up' also turns SWARD upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: On the football pools, tied matches are the results a gambler needs to occur.

clue.text: Forcefully stressing a chap has time to change

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are to change their order

explanation.surface: A man has the moment to alter his ways, and says so with force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges CHAP and TIME together into the answer; 'a' and 'has' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Said with emphasis, speech that is insistent and forceful.

clue.text: Make denial concerning my sweet consumption

parts.note: re means about, concerning
my eating of dessert: PUD (pudding) + I ATE

explanation.surface: Disclaim anything to do with my eating of pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: PUD is British slang for pudding (dessert), and 'my ... consumption' is I ATE, so the phrase reads PUD I ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown or reject something is to issue a denial of it.

clue.text: One crowded hour on the riverside

definitions.meaning: the busy time of day, the commuter hour
a reed-like plant growing by water

explanation.definitionFit: The busy commuting peak is the rush hour, and the marsh plant of that name grows along riverbanks.

clue.text: Mail French furniture in carriage

parts.note: post means mail
chaise is French for chair

explanation.surface: Sending a French chair by post inside a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-chaise was a hired horse-drawn coach for fast travel.

clue.text: Debt-collector gets nothing back from this bird

parts.note: a dun is someone who demands payment of a debt

indicators.note: back means the word for nothing is turned round

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A bailiff leaves this bird with nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The dunlin is a small wading sandpiper.

clue.text: Marble monument -fifth model, or the first

parts.note: Marble Arch is a London monument, so the Marble one is the ARCH
the models run A, B, C, D, E: the fifth is E-type

explanation.surface: A stone memorial, a fifth version, or the original.
explanation.walkthrough: Marble Arch is a triumphal arch in London; with models lettered A onwards, the fifth is the E-TYPE.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the original pattern from which copies derive, the prototype.

clue.text: Ten in tree-climbing exercise

indicators.note: in means one piece goes within the other
in a down light climbing means the word goes upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Ten people taking part in tree-climbing as a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns TREE upwards to EERT, and 'in' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert a force or influence is to exercise it.

clue.text: Start retreat — "very quietly" is in their order

indicators.note: in signals one piece inside the other
retreat means the word goes backwards

parts.note: pp (pianissimo) is the musical mark for very quietly

explanation.surface: A retreat begins in a monastery whose rule is silence.
explanation.walkthrough: Trappist monks keep a rule of near-total silence, so 'very quietly' fits the surface as well as giving the musical mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cistercians of the Strict Observance are monks of a religious order known for silence.

clue.text: Crane savaged Pearl's mum

indicators.note: savaged means the letters are mauled into a new order

explanation.surface: A wading bird attacks the mother of a girl named Pearl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pearl's mum' is mother-of-pearl, not a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl is the iridescent shell lining that forms pearls.

clue.text: Yoke up horses at hostelry outside Bath for instance

indicators.note: outside means the inn wraps around the spa

parts.note: an inn is a hostelry
Bath is an English spa town

explanation.surface: Harnessing horses at an inn just beyond the city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city famous for its Roman spa. INSPAN is South African English for harnessing a team.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspan is a South African word for harnessing draught animals to a wagon.

clue.text: Setting of cowboy films

parts.note: read as a film location, but meaning the region of the sunset, the West where Westerns happen

explanation.definitionFit: The West is where the sun sets and where Westerns are set.

clue.text: Here's one principal nonconformist leader

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
arch means chief, principal, as in archenemy

explanation.surface: Introducing a chief Dissenting minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A heresiarch founds or leads a heretical sect, a rebel against orthodoxy.

clue.text: Bloodsucking type of adventuress, one about to have her innings ?

parts.note: a vamp is a seductive adventuress
I is the Roman numeral one
re means about
to bat is to have one's innings in cricket

explanation.surface: A predatory seductress waits for her turn at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: An innings is a turn batting in cricket, so to have one's innings is to BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The vampire bat of the Americas feeds on blood.

clue.text: Poor sort of cheese for Hamlet's entertainment

definitions.meaning: cheap, mediocre cheese is called by the name of what it is used to bait
the play-within-a-play Hamlet stages for Claudius

explanation.definitionFit: Cheap cheese fit only for baiting rodents bears that name, and Hamlet titles his play for the court so.

clue.text: This New Army she's reorganized

indicators.note: reorganized means the letters of the word are re-ordered

explanation.surface: A woman has overhauled the forces into a new army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This New' and 's' only set the scene; 'reorganized' rearranges ARMY into a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Myra is a woman's given name, so a she.

clue.text: Bunthorne reveals how 'to shine in the high -line

definitions.text: Bunthorne reveals how 'to shine in the high -line

parts.words: Bunthorne reveals how 'to shine in the high -line
parts.note: fill the gap in Bunthorne's song in Gilbert and Sullivan's Patience: 'If you're anxious for to shine in the high ... line'

explanation.definitionFit: Bunthorne, a poet satirising the art-for-art's-sake movement, sings of the high artistic line.

clue.text: Bird-spaniel also you say ?

indicators.note: you say signals that the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: a cocker is a spaniel, and also means too

explanation.surface: A bird dog, as well, so you claim.
explanation.walkthrough: COCKER TOO, said aloud, sounds like the parrot's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatoo is a crested parrot.

clue.text: Party in utter defeat

definitions.meaning: an old word for a large evening gathering

explanation.definitionFit: A rout was an 18th-century term for a crowded reception, and it is also a disorderly flight after a beating.

clue.text: Chelsea residents worried — is one right to go after birds ?

indicators.note: to go after means this piece is placed after the birds

parts.note: pens are female swans

indicators.note: worried means the letters are troubled into a new order

explanation.surface: Locals in Chelsea are anxious about whether a right-winger should chase the girls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' scrambles the fodder and 'to go after' sets it behind the swans. The Chelsea Pensioners are retired soldiers living at the Royal Hospital in Chelsea, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Army veterans housed at London's Royal Hospital in Chelsea are known as the Chelsea Pensioners.

clue.text: In' France one is getting on-agreement noted

parts.note: un is French for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: In France, one gets along: harmony on record.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, voices in unison sing the same note together, so they agree.

clue.text: Plank-fixer, even inside the track

indicators.note: inside means the poetic word goes within the path

e'en is the poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: A carpenter's nail, and the path, even within.
explanation.walkthrough: E'EN is the old poetic form of 'even', common in hymns and verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A treenail is a wooden peg used to fasten planks in shipbuilding.

clue.text: No liner, though a lady in the song

definitions.meaning: a cargo ship that runs no scheduled route, as a liner does
from the song The Lady Is a ...

explanation.definitionFit: A tramp steamer takes cargo wherever it can, unlike a scheduled ocean liner, and Rodgers and Hart's song says the lady is one.

clue.text: Design for some basket-chairs

indicators.note: some of means just part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: A drawing for some wicker seats.

clue.text: Do returning astronauts hit the atmosphere at this angle ?

parts.words: Do returning astronauts hit the atmosphere at this angle ?
parts.note: plays on a spacecraft coming back into the atmosphere; the term is a geometry word for an inward-pointing angle

clue.text: How pudding-race chieftain is ceremoniously served

definitions.text: How pudding-race chieftain is ceremoniously served
